page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.4xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance based on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to an even 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes 33 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction set extensions including AVX and AVX-512F. Network throughput is provisioned with a 5 Gbps baseline. There is no bundled local storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring cloud block storage attachments for operating system and application data.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the middle tier for multi-threaded workloads, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 13022.87 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 5885.0. Static web serving throughput reaches 7.93 GB/sec, and caching benchmarks demonstrate stable throughput with 11.76 million Redis SET operations per second. In contrast, single-threaded performance is constrained, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and reduced efficiency during single-threaded compression tasks. Memory bandwidth reaches 71.56 GB/sec for uncached read operations, aligning with typical middle-tier memory subsystems.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the ecs.g5.4xlarge offers balanced compute and memory density for horizontally scaled multi-threaded architectures. The absence of integrated ephemeral disks requires consideration of remote block volume latency and capacity planning. The instance is suited for enterprise web serving tiers, microservices clusters, continuous integration workers, and medium-scale relational databases.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 system provides 64 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage and lacks GPU acceleration, depending on network-attached storage for disk operations. Benchmark results indicate average multi-core throughput, static web serving throughput of 7.93 GB/sec, and 11.76 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core speed is lower compared to modern alternatives. The instance suits multi-threaded enterprise services, web application clusters, and general database hosting.
